title: Shared traits of living things
cards.0.p: All living things are made of cells, and the cell is the smallest unit of life. In multicellular organisms, cells form a layered order: cell → tissue → organ → system → organism.
cards.0.svg#6: The cell is the basis of them all
cards.0.key: In a single-celled organism, the cell is also the organism itself.
cards.1.h: Metabolism: building up and breaking down
cards.1.p: All the chemical reactions in a living thing are called metabolism. Building large molecules from small ones is called anabolism, and it uses energy. Breaking down large molecules is called catabolism. Digestion and respiration are examples, and they usually release energy.
cards.1.key: Metabolism is the sum of anabolism, the building reactions, and catabolism, the breakdown reactions.
cards.2.p: A cell cannot use the energy in food directly. It first loads this energy onto ATP molecules. When the cell does work, ATP splits into ADP and phosphate. A cell holds only a small amount of ATP, so ATP is made again all the time.
cards.2.key: When water breaks down ATP, ADP, phosphate and energy are released: ATP + water → ADP + P + energy.
cards.3.p: Every living thing feeds. Autotrophs make their own food, and heterotrophs take in ready-made food. Through respiration, the energy in food is passed to ATP. Through excretion, wastes such as carbon dioxide and urea are removed from the body.
cards.3.svg#9: food comes in, energy is used, waste goes out
cards.3.key: Plants also carry out respiration. Photosynthesis does not replace respiration.
cards.3.etk.soru: Sort each organism by how it gets food.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.1.2: It has chlorophyll. It makes its own food by photosynthesis.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.2.2: Fungi have no chlorophyll. They absorb ready-made food from their surroundings.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.5.2: Yeast is a fungus. It takes in ready-made sugar.
cards.3.once.soru: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis. Do they also carry out respiration?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: Photosynthesis makes food, and respiration passes the energy in that food to ATP. Every living plant cell respires, day and night.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: To use the energy in the food it makes, a plant must also carry out respiration.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Respiration goes on during the day too. Photosynthesis is faster in daytime, so respiration goes unnoticed.
cards.4.p: In asexual reproduction, a single parent produces offspring like itself. A bacterium dividing is an example. In sexual reproduction, two gametes join. A mule cannot reproduce but is still alive, because reproduction is needed for the species to continue, not the individual.
cards.4.key: Asexual reproduction is fast, and the offspring resemble the parent. Sexual reproduction gives high variety.
cards.4.once.soru: A bacterium reproduces by dividing in two. How do the offspring compare with the parent?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: The parent copies its genetic material and divides, so the offspring are like copies of the parent. This is called asexual reproduction.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Variety increases when the gametes of two parents join. Division makes copies.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: In division, both offspring get the same genetic material.
cards.5.p: Growth is an increase in mass as the number or size of cells increases. Development is the maturing of structures and functions. A seed becoming a seedling and a caterpillar becoming a butterfly are examples of development.
cards.5.key: Growth is an increase in amount. Development is maturing and gaining new abilities.
cards.5.once.soru: A salt crystal and a seedling both grow. What makes the seedling's growth different?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: The seedling processes nutrients in its cells and makes new cells. A crystal grows by adding matter to its surface and has no metabolism.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Speed is not the difference. Some crystals grow faster than seedlings.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: A crystal also gets bigger. The difference is in how the growth happens.
cards.6.p: Living things sense stimuli such as light, heat and touch, and respond to them. Pulling your hand away from a hot stove and a sensitive plant folding its leaves are examples. The response is often a movement.
cards.7.p: Even when outside conditions change, a living thing keeps inner conditions such as body temperature, blood sugar and water content within narrow limits. This is called homeostasis. Sweating in the heat and shivering in the cold are examples.
cards.7.key: Homeostasis is keeping the inner environment steady while the outside world changes.
cards.8.p: An adaptation is an inherited trait that raises an organism's chance of surviving and reproducing. Adaptations build up over generations through natural selection. The change over time in populations, groups of the same species living together, is called evolution.
cards.8.key: Individuals do not evolve. Populations evolve over generations.
cards.8.once.soru: A cactus's leaves have turned into spines. How does this help in the desert?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: With less leaf surface, less water is lost by transpiration. Spines also protect the plant from animals. Inherited fits like this are called adaptations.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: In a cactus, the green stem does the photosynthesis. Spines do not increase it.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Cacti grow slowly. The main job of the spines is to save water.
cards.9.p: Viruses are not cells. They are made of a protein coat with DNA or RNA inside it. They can multiply only inside a living cell, so they are considered to be between living and nonliving.
cards.9.key: Outside a cell, a virus acts like a nonliving thing. Inside a cell, it acts like a living thing.
cards.10.h: The scientific method: setting up an experiment
cards.10.p: A biologist first forms a hypothesis and tests it with an experiment. Only one factor is changed in the experiment. This is called the independent variable. The measured result is called the dependent variable. A control group makes comparison possible.
cards.10.key: A theory is a broad explanation, and a law describes a relationship. So a theory does not turn into a law over time.
cards.10.once.soru: You are testing how fertilizer affects plant height, and you gave one pot fertilizer. What do you do with the second pot?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: If everything is kept the same and only the fertilizer differs, the fertilizer causes any difference in height. The pot without fertilizer is the control group.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Then you can't compare with the no-fertilizer case, and you can't see the fertilizer's effect.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: If the plant species also changes, you can't know what caused the difference. Only one factor should change in an experiment.
cards.11.p: Some discoveries changed our lives completely. The cell was first seen in 1665, and the first vaccine was made in 1796. In the 1860s, people learned that germs cause disease. Penicillin was found in 1928, the structure of DNA was solved in 1953, and the human genome was read in 2003.
cards.11.svg#18: discoveries changed medicine and life span
cards.11.key: Vaccines and antibiotics deserve the most credit for longer average life spans.
cards.11.once.soru: Over the last 150 years, the average human life span has more than doubled. What deserves the most credit?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: In the past, many children died of infections. Vaccines and antibiotics largely prevented this. Clean water and hygiene also helped.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The telescope changed astronomy, but it had no direct effect on health.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: This invention changed industry. Discoveries in medicine are what lengthened life spans.
cards.12.p: Scientific research must also follow ethical rules. Informed consent is obtained from volunteers who take part in studies, and animal experiments need approval from an ethics committee. Making up data, altering data and passing off someone else's work as your own (plagiarism) are fraud.
cards.12.svg#12: being right isn't enough: be honest and respectful too
cards.12.key: Animal research follows the 3R principle: replace animals with other methods, reduce the number of animals, refine the conditions.
cards.12.once.soru: A researcher deletes two measurements from a table because they didn't give the expected result. What is this?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: Deleting an unwanted result is altering the data. Whatever the result, it must be reported as it is.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: Data cannot be deleted unless a measurement error is proven, because deleting it distorts the result.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Data cannot be picked to suit the researcher. It must be reported as it is.
cards.13.p:
• Living things are made of cells and form a layered order.
• They feed, carry out respiration and excretion, and use energy through ATP.
• They reproduce, grow, develop and respond to stimuli.
• They keep their inner balance through homeostasis. Populations adapt to their environment over generations.
• Science advances through hypotheses and controlled experiments.
quiz.0.q: A student is studying how music affects the number of fruits on tomato plants. Match each term with what it means in this experiment.
quiz.0.ciftler.3.1: Plants in the greenhouse with no music
quiz.0.e: The only factor changed in the experiment is music, and the measured result is the number of fruits. Everything except music is kept the same, and the greenhouse with no music is the control group.
quiz.1.q: Put each process in the right branch of metabolism.
quiz.1.e: Building large molecules from small ones is anabolism, and it uses energy. Making protein, glycogen, and glucose in photosynthesis are examples. Breaking down large molecules is catabolism. Digestion, respiration and the breakdown of fats are examples.
quiz.2.q: Match each example with the trait of life it shows.
quiz.2.e: Keeping the inner environment steady is homeostasis. Thick fur that makes survival easier is an inherited adaptation. The maturing of structures is development, offspring from a single parent is asexual reproduction, and bending toward light is a response to stimuli.
quiz.3.q: A muscle cell holds very little ATP at any moment, but a muscle can work for hours. Why?
quiz.3.o.0: ATP is constantly remade from ADP and phosphate
quiz.3.o.1: Muscle uses energy directly from glucose
quiz.3.o.2: ATP rejoins by itself after it splits
quiz.3.o.3: Muscle takes ready-made ATP from the blood
quiz.3.e: The energy released in respiration recharges ATP by adding phosphate to ADP. This cycle never stops.
quiz.3.y.1: A cell cannot use the energy in food directly. It must first pass this energy to ATP.
quiz.3.y.2: Adding phosphate to ADP takes energy, and that energy comes from respiration.
quiz.3.y.3: ATP is not carried between cells. Each cell makes its own ATP.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name: climb the levels, split ATP, and watch body temperature and a virus.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Start from a muscle cell and climb the levels one by one. Stop when you reach the heart.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: The heart is an organ. Muscle, nerve and connective tissue work together to do one job: pump blood.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The cell carries energy in a molecule called ATP, and ATP gives energy when a muscle contracts. Predict what will happen before you press play.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: What happens when ATP gives energy for a muscle to contract?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: The last phosphate leaves, and energy is released
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Only the last phosphate bond breaks, leaving ADP with two phosphates. Respiration recharges ATP by adding the phosphate back to this ADP.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Only ATP's last phosphate leaves. The adenine and ribose stay in place.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Adding phosphate takes energy. ATP loses a phosphate when it gives energy.
A:adimlar.2.metin: The cell builds large molecules from small ones. This is called anabolism (building). Join the glucose molecules and see what changes.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: Which one is an example of anabolism?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A large molecule is built from small ones, and ATP is used. This is anabolism. Making starch from glucose is anabolism too.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Digestion breaks down large molecules. This is breakdown, or catabolism.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy, so it is catabolism.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Change the outside temperature and look at the inside temperature. Then go to a snowy day, 0 °C or below.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: In the cold, shivering muscles make heat, and skin blood vessels narrow to cut heat loss. So the inside temperature still stays near 37 °C.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The lamp is above the plant. Move the lamp to the right and let the plant grow.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.ipucu: Move the lamp to the right and play again.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: The plant bent toward the light. The cells on the shaded side grow longer, so the stem turns toward the light.
A:adimlar.5.metin: One virus is outside a cell, and the other is next to a living cell. Which one multiplies?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Can a virus multiply on its own outside a cell?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A virus injects its genetic material into a cell and uses the cell's ribosomes and energy to make copies of itself. It has no metabolism of its own, so it can do nothing outside a cell.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A virus is not a cell, so it cannot divide.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A virus with no metabolism cannot multiply at all outside a cell.
A:kapanis.0: Living things are made of cells and form this order: cell → tissue → organ → system → organism.
A:kapanis.1: The cell uses energy through ATP: ATP → ADP + P + energy.
A:kapanis.2: Metabolism is made up of anabolism, the building reactions, and catabolism, the breakdown reactions. Anabolism uses energy.
A:kapanis.3: Keeping the inner environment steady through responses such as sweating and shivering is called homeostasis.
A:kapanis.4: Living things respond to stimuli. Viruses can multiply only inside a living cell.
